document_title: 261 Minutes When No Flight Left Alaska
post_copy:
Flights within Alaska kept flying on November 13th while every flight leaving the state was grounded.

So said an Anchorage airport official. The FAA's nationwide stop ran 11:54 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Alaska time.

By mid-afternoon Cirium counted 670 flights sent back and 157 redirected nationwide. Three days earlier SMART, the FAA's AI traffic advisor, went national. The FAA blamed a router overloading older equipment. SMART's maker says the stop wasn't a result of its system.

The carousel shows the stop minute by minute, the national toll, SMART's rollout, the stated cause and Anchorage Center's airspace.

Should the next federal dollar go to the AI the FAA credits with 10 minutes per reroute or to the older equipment a router overloaded?

#AlaskaAviation #AirTrafficControl #AviationAI

slides.headline: For 261 minutes, no flight left Alaska.
labels: NOVEMBER 13TH, 11:54 A.M. TO 4:15 P.M. ALASKA TIME

slides.headline: At 11:54 a.m., the FAA stopped departures nationwide.
slides.body: Every flight leaving the state sat, an Anchorage airport official said. Flights inside Alaska kept flying. The FAA lifted the stop at 4:15 p.m. Alaska time, on Friday, November 13th.

slides.headline: By mid-afternoon, 827 flights had turned back or diverted.
slides.body: Cirium counted 670 flights sent back to where they took off and 157 redirected to another airport, nationwide. Reportedly only the second all-flight grounding since 9/11.

slides.headline: Three days earlier, the FAA's AI went national.
slides.body: SMART, an AI traffic advisor built by Air Space Intelligence, launched around Washington on September 21st. On November 10th it went live in the airspace of all 22 air route traffic control centers. House Democrats had asked GAO for an audit on October 13th.

slides.headline: The FAA blamed a router. The AI's maker saw no link.
slides.body: "A router sent too much data, overloading older air traffic control equipment." "Not based on or a result of the SMART system." "No indication" of a link to the new computer system.
labels: SO WHAT IS THE NEW AI COUNTED IN?

slides.headline: The new AI is counted in minutes saved. The stop took hours.
labels: 10 MINUTES, AVERAGE SAVED PER REROUTED FLIGHT, PER THE FAA 180 FLIGHTS REROUTED SO FAR
TWO SEPARATE EVENTS. OFFICIALS SAW NO INDICATION OF A LINK.

slides.headline: Inside Alaska, the clock kept running.
2,427,971 square miles of airspace.
slides.body: The FAA's most northern and western en route center. Its own automation, ATOP and MEARTS. Six foreign neighbor centers, in Japan, Russia and Canada.
labels: ANCHORAGE AIR ROUTE TRAFFIC CONTROL CENTER, PER THE FAA
THE RECORD DOES NOT SAY WHETHER SMART RUNS HERE

editor_notes_for_email: This edition picks up from No.36 (August 18th), which introduced SMART and Alaska Airlines' Flyways; this one covers the November 10th nationwide switch on and the November 13th ground stop. No fetched source places Anchorage Center among the 22 SMART centers, so the caption, the slides and the sources comment never say SMART runs over Alaska. The 4:15 p.m. Alaska time is the conversion of the FAA's 8:15 p.m. Eastern lift as NBC News reported it. 261 minutes (11:54 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. AKST) and 827 flights (670 plus 157) are declared aggregates of sourced figures, re-derived by aggregate_check. The 670 and the 157 are Cirium's nationwide counts at one moment in the midafternoon, not Alaska counts. Session effort read medium, although the repo settings carry high.
